title: Timestamped cosign attestations and promotion rules for model profile manifests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Current CI publishes model artifacts and performance profiles without a standard cryptographic timestamp or consistent promotion guardrails. This causes uncertainty when backtracking releases (no reliable notion of when an attestation was made), and makes automated promotion rules brittle across regions/tiers. Motivation: add verifiable, timestamped attestations using cosign + rekor transparency logging and codify promotion rules (canary traffic fractions, perf thresholds, time-gated promotion) into the release broker so onboarding is auditable and rollback-safe. Goal: deliver a CI pipeline change that 1) cosign-signs both model artifact bundles and profile manifests with timestamping, 2) writes entries to a transparency log, 3) uploads signed manifests to the profile-catalog, and 4) triggers a promotion workflow that enforces configurable acceptance criteria before full rollout.
acceptance_criteria: CI produces cosign signatures for model artifact tarballs and associated perf-profile JSON with RFC3161-like timestamping or equivalent rekor-backed timestamp
Signed artifacts and manifests are verifiable by the release-broker service using cosign/rekor public roots and return a deterministic verification result
Promotion workflow enforces: canary start (N concurrent shards), perf thresholds (latency P95 and cost/unit within X% of baseline), and minimum canary duration before auto-promote
Automatic fallback: if verification fails or perf regressions exceed thresholds, the promotion is aborted and a rollback path is triggered with notification to owners
All steps emit structured logs and linkable audit entries in the console (PRD/Runbook links) for SRE/Compliance review
technical_notes: Approach: extend existing model-onboard CI job to run cosign sign on both the artifact bundle and the perf-profile manifest. Use cosign's --timestamp-upload (or local RFC3161 TSP proxy) and ensure rekor entries are created. Add a new 'signed_manifest' field to the profile-catalog object storing signature metadata and rekor index. The release-broker will add a verifier step that fetches the signature, validates against pinned root keys (KMS-backed) and checks rekor consistency. Promotion rules will be expressed as a simple JSON policy attached to the manifest (example: {"canary_fraction":0.1,"min_duration_minutes":60,"perf_checks":[{"metric":"p95_latency_ms","max_increase_pct":10}] }). Edge cases: offline/on-prem customers where rekor access is blocked — support an alternative TSP flow with customer-provided timestamping authority and an indicator in the manifest that rekor was not used. Rollback plan: release-broker stores previous pinned manifest and can revert traffic routing in <5m. Backcompat: if a manifest lacks signature, it should be rejected for hosted and Dedicated lanes but allowed with warning for Private (per security policy).
